points.headline: Frontier LLM prices fell by up to 80% in a few months.
points.body: OpenAI and Anthropic cut API prices sharply, and analysts now treat cheap tokens as the new normal rather than a promotion. Developers are told to revisit model routing, caching and self-hosting choices, while IBM's CEO says open-weight models are now good and cheap enough to run on-prem.

points.headline: The PHP meltdown shows AI is shrinking the time from bug to exploit.
points.body: PHP patched two critical remote-code-execution flaws that attackers were already using, and coverage says AI tools made them faster to weaponize at internet scale. In the same week, researchers showed an autonomous attack agent that hijacks other models to do its work, and Microsoft pitched an AI security operations center for agent-speed attacks.

points.headline: Doubts grow about the payoff of the AI buildout.
points.body: An Apollo economist says AI has delivered zero financial payoff to most companies, and TechCrunch now keeps a running list of failed AI startups. Commentators call the data-center spend the largest bet in the history of capitalism, while local opposition and slow permitting delay new sites in the US and UK.

points.headline: Money keeps flowing into robot foundation models.
points.body: Eka Robotics raised $150M for a vision-force-action model and Dream Labs raised a $90M seed to build a general brain for everyday robots. Industry is moving too: Teradyne partners with Sereact on physical AI for logistics, Schaeffler opens a Chinese factory where humanoids will build humanoids, and Misumi launches a $50M robotics fund.

points.headline: Pushback against AI content gets more formal.
points.body: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads, and r/opensource banned AI-generated posts. Coverage also shows Google's AI search reshaping online publishing, and a test where Grok's model picks Republicans while OpenAI's picks Democrats raises new questions about model bias.

points.headline: Agent engineering shifts from demos to reliability.
points.body: Practitioners focus on context engineering, guardrails and agents that keep answering after their tools fail, while many new arXiv papers benchmark agent harnesses, retries and failure attribution. On the tooling side, the MCP C# SDK 2.0 makes HTTP stateless by default, and Google says Gemini 4 Argon optimized its 200K-line Agent Development Kit overnight.
